meta.title: About Andes
meta.description: Building the new foundation of the Latin American economy. The two-layer architecture of Agentic Commerce, the phase roadmap, and the team.

vision.title: Where we're headed
vision.lead: Building the new foundation of the Latin American economy.
vision.body: LATAM GDP is $6T. We aim to route 1–2% of it through our own infrastructure. As Agentic Commerce takes off globally in 2026, LATAM AC has to evolve as something distinct. Andes builds that base layer. A hundred-year company, born in Brazil.

two_layer.title: The two-layer architecture of Agentic Commerce
two_layer.lead: To complete AC, two layers are required — neither of which the giants can build.

layer1.title: Buying Agent
layer1.body: Uses global AI as the LLM and owns the touchpoint with LATAM consumers. This is the branding layer; being replaced by a giant here is acceptable.

layer2.title: Platform
layer2.body: Logistics, tax, legal, customs, ERP, accounting. The knowledge of LATAM ground reality cannot be built by incumbents. This is where the real value lives.

phase.title: Phase roadmap
phase.lead: AC for LATAM gets built in five steps.

team.title: Team
team.lead: A small, AI-leveraged team built around a vision-driven Founder paired with an Architect who structures it.

group.title: Group structure
group.desc: Andes Inc. (JP) governs IP and capital; through Andes BR, J-Planet runs the business on the ground.

meta.title: Businesses
meta.description: Andes' implementation of Agentic Commerce: J-Planet (cross-border EC), J-Vita (healthcare), and the LATAM AC Protocol.

jplanet.title: J-Planet
jplanet.lead: Japanese and Korean quality delivered to Brazilian consumers through WhatsApp.
jplanet.body: Phase 1 launches 2026-06-01. The full Japanese catalog goes live, and the WhatsApp agent experience runs purchase, payment, and delivery as one integrated flow.

jvita.title: J-Vita
jvita.lead: Japanese-quality healthcare brought to Brazil through Mandato personal imports.
jvita.body: Phase 0a launches 2026-06-01. GLP-1, hair growth, hormones, and weight management. J-Medical Ltda (in formation) operates the consumer brand.

protocol.title: LATAM AC Protocol
protocol.lead: In 2028, we release the shared infrastructure for Agentic Commerce in LATAM as OSS.
protocol.body: PIX, NF-e, ICMS, LGPD, and CDC turned into MCP — putting Andes in the position the giants (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) call into. The AWS, Stripe, and Rakuten of LATAM.

hero.title: A motion shelf for Andes.
hero.lead: A preview site that gathers the current animation kit and existing motion components in a form that can be moved into the Andes production site. It is a material shelf, focused on where each motion pattern should be used.

beam.title: Agent Beam
beam.description: A light path between nodes. For Andes, the strongest use is abstractly showing the connection between AI, brands, consumers, tax, and customs.

ticker.title: Number Ticker
ticker.description: A one-shot number reveal. Use it only for grounded numbers such as macro scale, launch year, and process steps.

particles.title: Particle Field
particles.description: A low-density particle background. Better as depth inside a dark section or corridor diagram than as a decorative full-page effect.

native.title: Native Andes Motion
native.description: Lightweight motion already used in the main site. These pull reusable patterns out of the hero, How it works, and Numbers sections.

fluid.title: Hero Fluid Lab
fluid.description: A larger direction check before adopting three-fluid-fx. In the hero, this should not feel like red paint; it should sit quietly inside the Navy depth and react with restraint.
fluid.note: Crimson stays pinpoint. Do not turn the whole background red.

gallery.reviewLead: Review the large preview, production fit, source, and adoption notes in one place.
gallery.motionStage1: Create a clear visual starting point
gallery.motionStage3: Keep meaning in the static state
gallery.implementationReady: Ready to move as an existing component. Keep it scoped to the section that needs it.
gallery.implementationPrototype: Candidate or research material. Validate texture, weight, and readability in preview first.
gallery.implementationReview: Not a motion component. Use it as a taste check before moving Vault items into production.
gallery.reducedMotionStatic: Provide a static state that still communicates when animation is disabled.
gallery.reducedMotionPause: High-motion or heavier candidate. Pause it or switch to a static fallback for reduced-motion users.

frontier.title: New references, translated for Andes.
frontier.lead: External skills and flashy examples go into the shelf with purpose and weight separated. This section is the entry point for the next prototypes.

gsapOfficial.label: GSAP
gsapOfficial.title: Use official gsap-skills as the motion playbook.
gsapOfficial.body: A reference set for writing Timeline, ScrollTrigger, Flip, SplitText, and SVG motion correctly. For Andes, keep it focused on hero typography and scroll narrative quality.

webglGlsl.label: WebGL / GLSL
webglGlsl.title: Make 3D an abstract economic space, not a realistic scene.
webglGlsl.body: Translate terrain, fog, depth of field, and scroll-driven camera ideas into Andes terrain, fluid depth, and corridor atmosphere.

splineReference.label: Spline
splineReference.title: Spline is a reference, not the first production choice.
splineReference.body: It is useful for quickly showing a 3D object, but the runtime can be heavy for a corporate hero. Prefer a lighter Three.js implementation first.

designTaste.label: Taste Guard
designTaste.title: Aesthetic guardrails against AI-looking motion.
designTaste.body: Use Frontend Design and Hallmark-style standards as Andes rules: restraint, two-color discipline, Crimson as a pinpoint, and motion with a clear job.

inventory.title: Motion patterns ready to pull.
inventory.lead: The shelf separates ported materials, existing components, and preview references. Pull only the motion that serves a production section.

beam.name: Animated Beam
beam.fit: Shows the flow of agentic commerce without becoming a noisy technical diagram. Useful for connecting Layer 1 and Layer 2.

ticker.name: Number Ticker
ticker.fit: Raises grounded numbers such as 660 million people or the 2026 launch. Best for investor-facing proof sections.

particles.name: Particle Field
particles.fit: Adds depth to a quiet dark canvas. Keep it in Navy and Paper tones, with Crimson reserved for point accents.

reveal.name: Reveal
reveal.fit: Fade and rise when a section enters the viewport. Use it for headings and key moments, not every card.

countUp.name: CountUp
countUp.fit: Extracts the numeric part from an i18n string and counts once without breaking prefixes or units.

smoothScroll.name: Lenis SmoothScroll
smoothScroll.fit: Improves the page scroll feel. It turns off for reduced-motion users.

maskedHeroType.name: Masked Hero Type
maskedHeroType.fit: Hero lines rise from a mask. Strong fit for the declarative Andes hero voice.

heroArc.name: Hero Corridor Arc
heroArc.fit: Draws a single JP/KR to BR arc with framer-motion pathLength, giving geography without a literal map.

scrollHint.name: Scroll Hint
scrollHint.fit: A thin line at the bottom of the hero breathes gently. Minimal cue for the next section.

networkFlow.name: Network Flow
networkFlow.fit: A dashed line flows while a node pulses. Already used in the four-step How it works flow.

productScene.name: Product Scene Cycle
productScene.fit: Ghost product cards float in cycles. Good for evidence sections away from the production hero.

progressFill.name: Progress Fill
progressFill.fit: A progress bar fills cyclically. Useful for logistics, budget, customs, or delivery state.

gaugeRing.name: Gauge Ring
gaugeRing.fit: Animates circular gauge stroke-dashoffset. Small way to show completion or budget change.

cssFadeUp.name: CSS Fade Up
cssFadeUp.fit: A small Tailwind motion-safe fade-up. Useful, but easy to overuse.

arc.name: Line / Arc Draw
arc.fit: Fits a single JP/KR to BR corridor line. A minimal geography cue that can support the hero declaration.

lineArcDraw.name: Line / Arc Draw
lineArcDraw.fit: SVG dashoffset line drawing. Works for corridor arcs, layer diagrams, and roadmap paths.

scrollMorph.name: Scroll Morph
scrollMorph.fit: A Revolut-style scroll morph from the preview. Too strong for the Andes production hero, but useful for product demo studies.

gsapSplit.name: GSAP SplitText / SplitType
gsapSplit.fit: Splits type into lines or characters for more precise hero typography. The preferred docs/09 direction.

gsapScrollTrigger.name: GSAP ScrollTrigger
gsapScrollTrigger.fit: Useful for section pinning, scrubbed progress, and staged line drawing. Prototype before production.

gsapOfficialSkills.name: GSAP Official Skills
gsapOfficialSkills.fit: Official skills that teach agents the GSAP playbook. Installing them should improve Timeline, React, and ScrollTrigger implementation quality.

gsapTimeline.name: GSAP Timeline
gsapTimeline.fit: Coordinates entrances, lines, numbers, and CTAs on one timeline. Better texture than stacking manual delays.

gsapFlip.name: GSAP Flip
gsapFlip.fit: Turns card rearrangement and state changes into natural movement instead of abrupt disappearance. Strong for product demos.

gsapMotionPath.name: GSAP MotionPath
gsapMotionPath.fit: Moves dots or labels along a corridor path. Shows logistics, payment, and customs flow without a literal map.

gsapSvgMorph.name: GSAP SVG Morph / Draw
gsapSvgMorph.fit: Stages SVG lines and shapes. Avoid loud morphing; use it for lines that grow and diagrams that clarify.

gsapPerformance.name: GSAP Performance Pass
gsapPerformance.fit: A quality pass for transform and opacity animation, cleanup, and ScrollTrigger refresh. Required as motion gets richer.

dreiFluidFallback.name: drei Gradient + Distort
dreiFluidFallback.fit: Safe fallback for a fluid hero background: quieter and lighter than a full fluid simulation.

threeFluidFx.name: three-fluid-fx
threeFluidFx.fit: Cursor-following fluid simulation. Needs quality and FPS validation before production.

webglMountainScene.name: WebGL Abstract Terrain
webglMountainScene.fit: Translate the mountain-scene idea into an abstract economic terrain for Andes. Better as a deep background plane than a realistic scene.

glslFogDepth.name: GLSL Fog Depth
glslFogDepth.fit: A shader that creates distance between layers like fog between peaks. Adds depth without adding more content.

lenisCameraScroll.name: Lenis Camera Scroll
lenisCameraScroll.fit: The camera physically advances with scroll. Use only when sections need to read as chapters.

webglDepthOfField.name: WebGL Depth of Field
webglDepthOfField.fit: Softens far objects and keeps hero copy forward. Likely desktop-only because postprocessing can get heavy.

scrollFogDensity.name: Scroll-linked Fog Density
scrollFogDensity.fit: Changes fog or fluid density with scroll progress. Gives motion feedback while keeping readability first.

twoColorWebglScene.name: Two-color WebGL Scene
twoColorWebglScene.fit: Restrains the palette to two colors and lets 3D depth carry the emotion. Matches Andes Navy / Paper / Crimson pinpoint discipline.

remotionStory.name: Remotion Agent Story
remotionStory.fit: Turns agentic chat flow into video. Safer as rendered video assets than an embedded player.

sierraStage.name: Sierra Feature Stage
sierraStage.fit: Scenario stage, progress, and product UI switching inspired by Sierra-style pages.

cinematicCanvas.name: Cinematic Canvas
cinematicCanvas.fit: Canvas and cinematic layer experiments. Too strong for production today, useful as background research.

logoMarquee.name: Logo Marquee
logoMarquee.fit: Horizontal wordmark motion. Use sparingly for press or partner strips.

videoLoop.name: Hero Video Loop
videoLoop.fit: Background video loop and Ken Burns reference for photographic heroes.

splineHeroObject.name: Spline Hero Object
splineHeroObject.fit: A fast way to place a 3D object in a hero. For Andes production, validate runtime weight and brand fit first.

splineScrollDrive.name: Spline + ScrollTrigger
splineScrollDrive.fit: A study lane for scroll-driven 3D examples. Translate cars and products into abstract platform objects.

frontendDesignSkill.name: Frontend Design Skill
frontendDesignSkill.fit: A design skill for avoiding generic AI layouts. For Andes, use it to create structural difference, not decoration.

hallmarkAestheticGuard.name: Hallmark Aesthetic Guard
hallmarkAestheticGuard.fit: The local standard against purple gradients and AI templates. Keeps Andes corporate motion restrained.

aiMotionTasteRubric.name: AI Motion Taste Rubric
aiMotionTasteRubric.fit: A selection rule for whether motion feels like a slide deck, has meaning, and has texture. Use before moving Vault items into production.

restrain.title: Motion only where it means something.
restrain.body: Limit motion to the hero, numbers, connection lines, and key CTAs. Do not keep the whole page in motion.

tokens.title: Crimson stays pointed.
tokens.body: Do not turn Crimson into a large surface or particle field. Use Andes Crimson for lines, dots, and active states.

reducedMotion.title: Reduced motion is part of the component.
reducedMotion.body: Particles, numbers, and beams must still communicate when motion is disabled. The static state has to carry the information.

hero.scale: An economy of 660 million people starts here.
hero.subhead: Andes is the agentic commerce platform that carries Japanese and Korean brands to 660 million people across Latin America. Behind the conversation, Andes runs logistics, payments, tax, and customs.

services.bentoTitle: Every brand. Every way to sell.
services.bentoLead: Payments, logistics, tax, and customs in one toolkit — built to work alone or together.
services.tileAgentBody: Just talk on WhatsApp. No search, no cart — the agent picks, orders, and tracks delivery.
services.tileTaxBody: CIF, II, and ICMS handled behind the conversation. The hard cross-border math, made invisible.
services.tileLogiTitle: From pickup to doorstep in 4–7 days.
services.tileLogiBody: From Japan and Korea to Brazil, customs included — bundled into one path.
services.tilePayTitle: PIX and NF-e, from day one.
services.tilePayBody: Local payments via PIX and electronic invoicing via NF-e, built in. Plugged straight into local commerce.
services.tileErpTitle: Inventory and accounting, on the agent.
services.tileErpBody: Phase by phase — ERP, accounting, and credit.
services.infraLead: The top layer uses the world's AI to face brands and consumers. The lower layer roots deep in the region — infrastructure no one else can build. The real value is in the lower layer.
services.layer1Desc: Uses the world's AI as an LLM; owns the brand and consumer touchpoint
services.layer2Desc: Logistics, tax, legal, customs, ERP, fintech — Andes's own deep infrastructure
services.endgame: In 2028, we issue Latin America's shared infrastructure as a protocol.
services.tileDashTitle: Every brand's sales, on one platform.
